answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a locked stake that is slashed when two identities are traced to one controller. A bridge between proof-of-personhood and the ledger lets a meadow of fresh agents be checked against that bond; each fake lotus must fund its own stake, so the attacker pays linearly per identity while the reward per identity stays fixed, making a large Sybil farm uneconomical.
